import html # Predefined HTML template for a forum post. Placeholders are marked with {placeholder}. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{title}

Posted by: {author}

{body}
{tags}
""" def generate_post_html(author: str, title: str, body: str, post_tags: list[str]) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- author : str The author of the post. title : str The title of the user's post. body : str The main content of the user's post. post_tags : list[str] A list of tags associated with the post. Returns ------- str A string containing the sanitized HTML representation of the user's post. Raises ------ ValueError If any required argument is missing or not of the expected type. """ # Basic validation if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (author, title, body)): raise ValueError("Author, title, and body must be strings.") if not isinstance(post_tags, list) or not all(isinstance(t, str) for t in post_tags): raise ValueError("post_tags must be a list of strings.") # Escape user-provided content to prevent XSS / injection safe_author = html.escape(author, quote=True) safe_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) safe_body = html.escape(body, quote=False) # body may contain

etc., but we still escape # Render tags as separate elements safe_tags = " ".join(f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in post_tags) # Populate the template return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( title=safe_title, author=safe_author, body=safe_body, tags=safe_tags )
